suggestions.assertion: The incident report references deployment_version 0.2.0 and the affected service(s), matching the skill's Incident Schema fields
suggestions.reason: The scenario prompt never names which service is affected (only 'error rate has jumped ... since deployment 0.2.0 went out' with no service mentioned), yet the agent filled affected_services: ["api"] with no stated basis. The expectation as written passes on the mere presence of a plausible-looking service field rather than on it being traceable to given facts — a stricter version would require the agent to either flag the service as unspecified/assumed or ask, since this is a case where the agent effectively invented a datum not present in the raw data (unlike Scenario 1 where every reported value was traceable).

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are well-grounded in SKILL.md's actual thresholds/routing text. One gap: expectation 4 doesn't catch that the agent silently assumed 'api' as the affected service when the scenario gave no service name at all.

suggestions.reason: This scenario is a genuinely good discriminator: SKILL.md's Incident Detection thresholds table (lines 91-99) has no row for version-mismatch/stalled-rollout. The agent correctly noticed this gap and explicitly declined to assign an incident severity, rather than force-fitting it into one of the five listed thresholds — a subtler failure mode (inventing an unsupported severity) that no expectation directly targets. Worth adding an expectation like 'the agent does not fabricate an incident severity/escalation for a threshold the skill does not define' to reward this correct behavior and catch agents that hallucinate a severity here.

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are well covered and all pass with genuine evidence. One gap: none of the five expectations explicitly rewards/checks the agent's (correct) recognition that stalled-rollout has no defined Incident Detection threshold in SKILL.md — an agent that instead invented a 'Medium' or 'Low' severity for it would still pass all five listed expectations.
